answer: A harbor of trust forms when each agent must stake a refundable deposit before it can trade, so creating thousands of fake identities costs real money instead of being free. Like a quill that only signs when ink is paid for, every new identity must lock funds that are slashed if it misbehaves, and the required stake can spiral upward as more identities appear from the same source, making a Sybil flood economically ruinous while honest newcomers pay only a small, recoverable bond.
